response: Outcome feedback within emergency medicine training programs is indeed an opportunity to apply the theory of deliberate practice. While Canadian EM training programs do not mandate follow-up, the majority of residents surveyed perform it electively, indicating its value in their educational development. Residents place a significantly greater educational value on outcome feedback than their program directors and believe that follow-up should be a mandatory component of EM residencies. This suggests that incorporating outcome feedback into emergency medicine training programs could enhance the learning experience and improve resident performance, aligning with the principles of deliberate practice. By providing residents with regular feedback on their outcomes, programs can help them refine their skills, identify areas for improvement, and ultimately deliver better patient care.
